    // Where the contour crosses cell edge e: the linear interpolation of the
    // edge's two corner positions at the parameter where the corner values reach
    // isoLevel. Equal corner values carry no crossing information, so they fall
    // back to the edge midpoint.
    MarchingSquaresEdgePoint(edge: Integer, cell: IntegerVector2, valueAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Number>, pointAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Point2D>, isoLevel: Number)
        : Point2D
    {
        var a = edge;
        var b = (edge + 1) % 4;
        var va = MarchingSquaresCornerValue(cell, a, valueAt);
        var vb = MarchingSquaresCornerValue(cell, b, valueAt);
        var t = va == vb ? 0.5 : va.InverseLerp(vb, isoLevel);
        return MarchingSquaresCornerPoint(cell, a, pointAt)
            .Lerp(MarchingSquaresCornerPoint(cell, b, pointAt), t);
    }

    // The contour segments of one cell. Empty for the two uncut configurations.
    MarchingSquaresCell(table: Array<Integer>, cell: IntegerVector2, valueAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Number>, pointAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Point2D>, isoLevel: Number)
        : Array<Line2D>
    {
        var c = MarchingSquaresCase(cell, valueAt, isoLevel);
        var row = c * 4;
        return MarchingSquaresSegmentCount(table, c).MapRange(s =>
            Line2D(
                MarchingSquaresEdgePoint(table[row + s * 2], cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel),
                MarchingSquaresEdgePoint(table[row + s * 2 + 1], cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel)));
    }

    //==
    // # Marching squares — the lattice driver and entry points

    // The iso-contour at isoLevel through a scalar lattice of nodeCounts sampled
    // nodes, as unordered segments. `valueAt` reports the sample at a node and
    // `pointAt` its world position; both are called only with in-range indices.
    // A lattice of n nodes on an axis marches n - 1 cells, so an axis with fewer
    // than two nodes contributes nothing.
    //
    // Segments arrive in cell order, not walked into loops: chaining them into
    // closed polygons is a separate pass, and one that has to decide what to do
    // at the saddles.
    MarchingSquaresLattice(nodeCounts: IntegerVector2, valueAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Number>, pointAt: Function2<Integer, Integer, Point2D>, isoLevel: Number)
        : Array<Line2D>
    {
        var table = Line2D.MarchingSquaresCaseTable;
        var columns = (nodeCounts.X - 1).Max(0);
        var rows = (nodeCounts.Y - 1).Max(0);
        var cells = MapRange(columns * rows, n => IntegerVector2(n % columns, n / columns));
        return cells.FlatMap(cell => MarchingSquaresCell(table, cell, valueAt, pointAt, isoLevel));
    }

    // The iso-contour of a 2D scalar field over `domain`, sampled on a grid of
    // `resolution` nodes per axis. The boundary of the region where the field is
    // at or above isoLevel, to within the sampling resolution.
    // Preconditions: both resolution components exceed one.
    IsoContour(self: IScalarField2D, domain: Bounds2D, resolution: IntegerVector2, isoLevel: Number): Array<Line2D>
        => MarchingSquaresLattice(
            resolution,
            (i, j) => self.Eval(IsoContourNode(domain, resolution, i, j)),
            (i, j) => IsoContourNode(domain, resolution, i, j),
            isoLevel);

    // The world position of lattice node (i, j) of an iso-contour grid: the
    // domain corners are sampled, so node 0 sits on the low edge and node
    // resolution - 1 on the high edge.
    IsoContourNode(domain: Bounds2D, resolution: IntegerVector2, i: Integer, j: Integer): Point2D
        => domain.FromUnitSquare(Point2D(
            i.ToNumber / (resolution.X - 1).ToNumber,
            j.ToNumber / (resolution.Y - 1).ToNumber));

    //==
    // # ITimeVaryingVectorField3D
    //
    // A spatial vector field evolving over a timeline: fluid velocity, wind, and
    // turbulence used for advection.

    // The vector at the point at a given instant; a readable spelling of
    // EvalAtTime.
    VectorAtTime(self: ITimeVaryingVectorField3D, point: Point3D, time: Instant): Vector3D
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, time);

    // The flow speed at the point at a given instant: the sampled vector's length.
    MagnitudeAtTime(self: ITimeVaryingVectorField3D, point: Point3D, time: Instant): Number
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, time).Magnitude;

    // The change in the vector at the point from the earlier instant to the later.
    ChangeBetween(self: ITimeVaryingVectorField3D, point: Point3D, earlier: Instant, later: Instant): Vector3D
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, later) - self.EvalAtTime(point, earlier);
}
